Tags: [SbyVerilog] gives the three immediate statements inside always @(*) or a clocked always, the clocked-assertion one-step-earlier note, $past/$stable/$changed/$rose/$fell in clocked blocks only, and $past undefined in the first cycle; [YVerilog] gives assert in its most basic form (assert property (expr) in module scope, assert(expr) in an always block) with assume, restrict and cover under the same limits; [SbyVerific] says sequences, |-> and |=> properties and clocking belong to the Verific front end of the commercial Tabby CAD Suite; [ZFormal] says an assume is forced true and not proved, and shows the f_past_valid guard.

Run: eda_antecedents.derive on a small file gave a cover (1'b1) wrapped in place for an assertion inside an if in a clocked block, 'cover property (@(posedge clk) a);' after a module-scope 'a |-> b', and refusals with the reason for the '##' sequence operator, a nested implication ('an implication inside parentheses is not supported'), an action block, a deferred assertion and a named sequence, as the document lists.

parse_sby_cover: unreached own cover fails 'vacuous'; an unreached derived antecedent fails with 'assertion never checked'; no cover reached fails with 'a setup with nothing to reach says nothing about its assumptions'; a derived cover not in the elaborated design is a warning and does not fail (eda_parsers.py:413-415, 432-434).

Eval case sentence: evals/dv/formal_credit_counter.json (skills include sva) says 'Use the SVA subset open Yosys reads: immediate assertions, assumptions and covers in always blocks, with $past; no implication or sequence operators', which is the constraint the document says it states.

The document says whether an open build accepts a clocked 'assert property (@(posedge clk) a |-> b)' is decided by its front end and no run is recorded; that is a hedge, not a claim, and is marked unverified in gate_claims.

gate_claims.claim: formal.run runs a single-task setup and refuses one with [tasks]
given sources, every source must be listed under [files] of the setup
prove proves every property: proven is 1 only for a passing proof in prove mode
bmc shows no counterexample within the depth only, and the summary says it is not a proof
the failing assertion and its step are recorded in the diagnostics
formal.cover runs the same setup in mode cover, from a copy
formal.cover fails when any cover is never reached
formal.cover fails when no cover is reached, so a setup with none fails
a cover is derived for the guard of each assertion, and a run in which a guard is never reached fails because the assertion is then never checked
for an assertion inside procedural code the derived cover sits on the same path under every enclosing if, case arm and loop (checked by running derive)
for a module-scope A |-> B or A |=> B the derived cover is of A (checked by running derive)
the derivation refuses a sequence operator, a nested implication, a named sequence, an action block, a deferred assertion and a macro that cannot be expanded (checked by running derive)
the cover run is refused and lists each place it cannot derive
a setup that passes formal.run can still be refused by formal.cover
an assertion not in the elaborated design draws a warning that no proof checks it
